newsitem.title: USA: Tribe drops bid to stop Detroit casino planning.
newsitem.headline: Tribe drops bid to stop Detroit casino planning.

text.p: A Michigan Indian tribe announced Tuesday it has dropped a bid to halt the process for selecting Detroit casino developers while its lawsuit challenging them remains pending.
The Lac Vieux Desert Band of Lake Superior Chippewa Indians in July had asked a federal judge to enjoin the City of Detroit and Michigan Gaming Control Board from continuing with the licensing plans.
"The court has satisfied our concerns by scheduling an expedited review of the lawsuit," Tribal Chairman John McGeshick said in a statement.
Detroit Mayor Dennis Archer is scheduled to announce finalists for the three available licenses on Friday. Eleven groups have filed preliminary applications for licenses.
The tribe's request for an injunction had been set for a hearing Wednesday in federal court in Grand Rapids.
The tribe's lawsuit contends that preferences included in the law for backers of the legislation are unconstitutional.
